# devicebasedauth.org

> Revocable, device-bound authentication and authorization as a pay-as-you-go web service. A device (browser, phone, server, CLI, AI agent) keeps its own private key; devicebasedauth.org issues it a signed, human-readable credential listing exactly what it may do, on which site, when and where. Servers verify offline for free or ask online (metered) for instant revocation, usage limits and owner approval. Prepaid balance, no subscription.

Machine-readable API: https://devicebasedauth.org/openapi.json
Credential format: https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/credential.md
Grant evaluation rules and test vectors: https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/evaluation.md
Revocation webhook events: https://github.com/curtcox/device-based-auth/blob/main/spec/events.md
Docs: https://devicebasedauth.org/docs/
Everything in one file (this summary, every route, the credential spec, evaluation rules and pricing): https://devicebasedauth.org/llms-full.txt
MCP endpoint: POST https://devicebasedauth.org/mcp (Streamable HTTP; Authorization: ApiKey dbak_… or a device credential)

## Key facts

- Money is integer micro-dollars (µ$; $1 = 1,000,000 µ$). Every JSON response includes `cost_microdollars`. `GET /api/v1/quote?op=<op>` prices an operation before you do it.
- Prices (µ$): issue 75, renew 25, online decision 10, metered API read 5, token exchange 5, OIDC login 10 (paid by the site), audience registration/change 100. Offline verification, JWKS, status lists, revocation, inspection and the web dashboard are free.
- Errors: `{ "error": "...", "code": "..." }` with HTTP status; 402 = insufficient balance.
- Private keys never leave the device. The service only ever sees public keys.

## Credentials

A credential is a compact JWS (ES256), header `{"typ":"dba-device+jwt","alg":"ES256","kid":…}`. Decode the middle segment (base64url JSON) to read it:
`iss`, `sub` (device id), `acct` (issuing account), `aud` (site names), `cid` (credential id), `jti`, `iat`/`nbf`/`exp`, `cnf.jkt` (device key thumbprint), `device`, `grants`, `status.status_list {idx, uri}`, `ver`.

A grant: `{ "actions": ["hashbin:content:write"], "resources": ["*"], "when": {"tz","windows":[{"days","from","to"}],"not_before","not_after"}, "where": {"source":"network|device|both","countries","regions","areas":[{"lat","lon","radius_m"}],"networks"}, "limits": {"uses":{"count","per"},"spend_usd_per_month"}, "require": {"online","step_up"} }`. Deny by default; any passing grant allows; unknown constraints deny.

Present it as `Authorization: DBA <credential>` plus `DPoP: <proof>` (RFC 9449 proof JWT signed by the device key with htm, htu, iat, jti, ath).

## Verify (relying party)

```js
import { createVerifier } from '@devicebasedauth/verify';
const dba = createVerifier({ audience: 'example.com' });
const result = await dba.verifyRequest(request, { action: 'example:write', resource: 'doc-1' });
if (!result.allow) return new Response(result.code, { status: result.status });
// Grants with usage limits / step-up / require.online: dba.verifyOnline(request, check) with createVerifier({ online: { apiKey } }).
```

Offline verification fetches `https://devicebasedauth.org/.well-known/jwks.json` and status lists (`https://status.devicebasedauth.org/v1/lists/<n>`, signed JWT, bit idx set = revoked), caching both.

Instant offline revocation: set `revocation_webhook` (https on your audience's domain) with `PATCH /api/v1/audiences/{name}`. Revocations of credentials naming your audience arrive as a POSTed JWS (`typ: dba-event+jwt`, signed with the issuer key); `await dba.handleEvent(await request.text())` verifies it and makes the verifier deny those credentials at once. Retried after 1 min, 10 min, 1 h; free for audiences; the status list stays authoritative. `POST /api/v1/audiences/{name}/webhook-test` sends a test event (read price).

## Enroll a device

- Browser: `import { DBA } from 'https://devicebasedauth.org/sdk/dba.js'; const dba = new DBA(); await dba.enroll({ aud: ['example.com'], grants: [{ actions: ['example:write'] }] }); await dba.fetch(url)`.
- CLI / agent: `dba enroll --aud example.com --action example:write` prints an approval URL for the human owner, then polls. `dba curl …`, `dba token --aud example.com`, `dba renew`, `dba revoke`. The CLI renews automatically at 2/3 of the lifetime when it uses the credential (`--no-renew` or `DBA_AUTO_RENEW=0` to stop); `dba renew --if-due` suits cron.
- HTTP: `POST /api/v1/enrollments {request}` where request is a JWS (typ `dba-enroll+jwt`, the new public key in the header `jwk`) over `{iat, aud, grants, device, lifetime_seconds?}`. Response: `approval_url` (give it to the human), `poll_url`. Poll `GET poll_url` until `status` is `approved` (then `credential` is included), `denied` or `expired`.
- Android key attestation (optional): `POST /api/v1/enrollments/attestation-challenge` → `challenge`; generate the Keystore key with `setAttestationChallenge(challenge ASCII bytes)`; add `attestation: {format: "android-key", challenge, x5c: [base64 DER, leaf first]}` to the enrollment request payload. Verified chains put `device.attestation {format, security_level: tee|strongbox, verified_boot, device_locked, verified_at}` in the credential; a rejected chain is `400 invalid_attestation`. Sample: docs/samples/android.
- Fleets: the owner creates an enrollment token (`POST /api/v1/enrollment-tokens {name, aud, grants, lifetime_seconds, max_uses, expires_in_days}` → `token: dbae_…`, shown once). Each device signs its usual enrollment request (aud/grants optional; may only narrow the token's) and sends `POST /api/v1/enrollments/redeem {request, enrollment_token}` — issued at once, issue price charged to the token's account. CLI: `DBA_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN=dbae_… dba enroll`; SDK: `dba.enroll({}, { enrollmentToken })`.
- mTLS: `POST /api/v1/certificate {lifetime_seconds?}` (device credential + DPoP; 300–86400 s, default 3600; token price) returns a PEM X.509 client certificate for the device's own key, signed by the CA in `/.well-known/dba-ca.pem`; CN = device id, SAN URIs `urn:devicebasedauth:{device,credential,account}:…`; no grants, no revocation. CLI: `dba certificate` then `curl --cert client.crt --key client.key`.
- Pre-approved issuance: `POST /api/v1/credentials {public_jwk, aud, grants, device, lifetime_seconds}` with an API key holding `credentials:issue` (or a device credential holding `dba:credentials:issue`, which can only delegate narrower grants).

## Main endpoints

- `GET /api/v1/whoami` — who is calling.
- `GET /api/v1/credentials`, `GET /api/v1/credentials/{cid}` (grants in plain English), `DELETE /api/v1/credentials/{cid}` (revoke), `GET /api/v1/credentials/{cid}/decisions`.
- `GET /api/v1/devices`, `POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/revoke`, `POST /api/v1/revoke-all {"confirm":"revoke-all"}`.
- `POST /api/v1/credentials/{cid}/renew` (device credential + DPoP; `new_key_proof` to rotate keys), `POST /api/v1/token {audience}` (≤10-minute bearer token), `POST /api/v1/self/revoke`.
- `POST /api/v1/authorize {credential, proof, request:{method,url}, audience, action, resource, context:{network}}` — online decision for an audience you own.
- `POST /api/v1/inspect {credential, check?}` — decode, verify, check revocation, evaluate. Free.
- `GET|POST /api/v1/audiences` — relying parties and their action catalogs (`GET /api/v1/audiences/{name}/usage`: your audience's online decisions, sign-ins and spend per month); register your domain (prove it with `https://<domain>/.well-known/devicebasedauth.json` = `{"account":"<your account>"}`).
- `GET /api/v1/account`, `GET /api/v1/transactions`, `GET /api/v1/audit`, `GET|PATCH /api/v1/account/settings` (dashboard only: `max_issues_per_day`, default 500; `max_renewals_per_credential_per_month`, default no cap; beyond them the API answers 429 `issuance_limit` / `renewal_limit` and charges nothing).
- OpenID Connect: `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (authorization code + PKCE S256; client_id = audience name).

## API keys and scopes

Create keys in the dashboard (`dbak_…`, shown once). Scopes: `account:read`, `transactions:read`, `credentials:read`, `credentials:issue`, `credentials:revoke`, `audiences:read`, `audiences:write`, `authorize`. Send `Authorization: ApiKey dbak_…`. Key reads are metered (5 µ$); dashboard reads are free.

## First-party audiences

`devicebasedauth.org` (namespace `dba`), `hashbin.org` (`hashbin:*`, mirrors hashbin's API key scopes, e.g. `hashbin:content:write`), `cronly.org` (`cronly:read`, `cronly:run`, `cronly:change`, `cronly:prose`, `cronly:secrets:write`). `<ns>:session` means "may sign in to that site".
